title: When the Asset Wakes
premise: Dominic Eriksen, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of his family in row twelve of Flight 4471, is approached by a stranger named Vera Kade who claims he once saved her life — a favor he has no memory of. Vera is a former intelligence courier whose stolen memory archive holds the truth about row twelve: a targeted assassination disguised as mechanical failure, buried by the agency that trained her. As the agency's cleaners close in, Dominic must decide whether to trade the archive — the only proof his family was murdered — for the lives of the makeshift family of witnesses they've gathered along the way. In the end, Dominic chooses justice over vengeance, releasing the archive publicly at the cost of his official career, while Vera, the one person who remembers his forgotten favor, helps him build a new family from the wreckage.
about_author: Ansel Amberdale is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who spent a decade reconstructing accidents no one wanted explained. They write thrillers about ordinary people forced to break extraordinary rules, and live quietly near a regional airport.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Five years after the crash, Dominic works a routine investigation, still cataloging anomalies from Flight 4471 in a private notebook. A memorial visit ends with him reciting the passenger list like a prayer. Emotional beat: grief calcified into ritual, the wound that drives everything.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera Kade appears at Dominic's office door claiming he pulled her from a burning car in Oslo — an event he cannot remember. She leaves a burner phone and a warning: 'They're rewriting your file too.' Emotional beat: uncanny intrusion, the first crack in his ordered world.

chapters.title: Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic verifies the Oslo accident report: no rescue was ever recorded, and his own travel records for that week have been altered. Someone inside the system is editing him. Emotional beat: professional certainty curdling into paranoia.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera explains she is a retired courier whose memory archive — encoded recordings of everything she transported — includes a file labeled ROW TWELVE. She intends to repay the favor by giving it to him. Emotional beat: wary alliance, two people testing each other's lies.

chapters.title: The Cleaner
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A man named Sorrel, posing as an aviation board auditor, interviews Dominic about 'irregularities' in his casework. Dominic realizes the audit is a fishing expedition and hides the notebook. Emotional beat: the hunted feeling, rules turned into weapons.

chapters.title: What the Archive Says
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Vera decrypts a fragment: Flight 4471's cargo manifest was falsified to move a person, and row twelve was not random. She withholds the full file — it's her only leverage and her only insurance. Emotional beat: hope laced with the poison of partial truth.

chapters.title: Safe House Rules
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The two go dark in a borrowed safe house belonging to Vera's old handler, Marisol, a defector running a boarding house for burned operatives. Emotional beat: the first taste of found family — strangers cooking dinner while the walls have ears.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Counted
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Introduces Teodor, a teenage hacker witness to a related 'accident,' living under Marisol's protection. Teodor has independently flagged Flight 4471's black box anomalies. Emotional beat: Dominic seeing his grief mirrored in a child's obsession.

chapters.title: Sorrel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. The agency cleaner reports to Director Hale that Vera has resurfaced and the Eriksen file is compromised. Sorrel argues for containment; Hale orders retrieval of the archive 'intact.' Emotional beat: cold bureaucratic evil, the machine waking up.

chapters.title: The Oslo Lie
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Dominic presses Vera on the favor she owes. She admits the rescue never happened — the memory is a planted seed from her own archive, a message her past self left for her. Someone wanted them connected. Emotional beat: betrayal and its strange inverse, a lie that tells the truth.

chapters.title: Black Box
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. With Teodor's help, Dominic obtains a copy of the flight recorder data and confirms a depressurization event that matches no mechanical cause. The notebook and the data agree: row twelve was targeted. Emotional beat: vindication that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: Marisol's Price
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Hale's people find the safe house network. Marisol reveals she's been feeding the agency misinformation to protect her residents, but the noose is tightening — and she tells Dominic the archive has a second claimant. Emotional beat: the protector's terrible arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Second Claimant
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. The rival claimant is Elias Voss, Vera's former partner, presumed dead, who helped falsify the manifest and wants the archive destroyed. He contacts Vera directly with an offer: the archive for her life. Emotional beat: the past arriving with a gun.

chapters.title: Trade Route
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic proposes the unthinkable — trade the archive to Sorrel through back channels to buy the witnesses' safety, then rebuild the case from public records. Vera refuses; the archive dies with the trade. First real fracture between them. Emotional beat: justice versus leverage, love versus proof.

chapters.title: Teodor Taken
chapters.summary: Teodor's POV. Sorrel's team grabs Teodor during a supply run, using him as bait to force the archive handover in 72 hours. Emotional beat: guilt detonating — the found family's weakest member paying for the adults' war.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vera and Dominic plan an exchange that is actually an extraction, while Marisol calls in every favor she has left. Dominic confesses that if it comes down to Teodor or the truth, he chooses Teodor — his family already died once. Emotional beat: resolve forged in fear.

chapters.title: Exchange at the Hangar
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The handover at a decommissioned airfield goes wrong when Voss double-crosses everyone, intending to kill Vera, Sorrel, and the archive together. Dominic springs the extraction; Sorrel, betrayed, makes a split-second choice not to shoot. Emotional beat: chaos, and the first enemy defecting.

chapters.title: What Sorrel Knows
chapters.summary: Sorrel's POV. Cornered and cut loose by Hale, Sorrel reveals the order for row twelve came from above Hale — a state-level client — and that Hale plans to burn the entire operation, including Sorrel. Emotional beat: the instrument realizing it is disposable.

chapters.title: Hale's White Room
chapters.summary: Vera's POV. Captured during the escape, Vera is interrogated by Hale, who offers her a memory wipe — the agency's mercy — in exchange for the archive's location. She stalls, buying Dominic time. Emotional beat: memory as identity, and the threat of losing it.

chapters.title: The Public Ledger
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The climax: instead of a secret trade, Dominic and Teodor push the decrypted archive — row twelve evidence and the agency's domestic assassination program — to a coalition of journalists and aviation regulators simultaneously. Hale's containment collapses. Emotional beat: the gamble that truth, once loose, cannot be repossessed.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Annotated
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Hale is arrested by his own oversight board; Voss flees and is quietly erased by the state he served; Sorrel testifies in exchange for a new name. Vera is freed. The boarding house takes in another stray. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Favor, Repaid
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Months later, Dominic, barred from official investigation work, runs an independent accident-reconstruction practice with Teodor. Vera stays — not out of debt, she says, but choice. At a new memorial, he reads row twelve's names once, then closes the notebook. Emotional beat: memory honored by living, the found family complete.
